items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish.
lines: Narrator
That seventy percent off tag? The price it's off from may never have existed.
Narrator
Here's the trick. Right before a sale, the "was" price goes up.
Narrator
Nineteen ninety-nine rupees, crossed out. Now nine ninety-nine. You feel like you won.
Narrator
But say it sold for nine ninety-nine all last month anyway.
Narrator
Your brain anchors on the first number it sees. That's the whole game.
Narrator
So why don't shops get caught? Nobody had to show the real old price.
Narrator
That's changing. From January twenty twenty-seven, India's new rule puts the lowest price of the last thirty days next to every discount.
Narrator
Europe already has this rule. In an EU check of three hundred and fourteen online shops, about thirty percent still showed discounts wrong.
Narrator
That's the mirage: the discount isn't counted from the real price. It's counted from a made-up one.
Narrator
So ignore the crossed-out number. Check the price history.
Narrator
Sometimes the best deal was always this price.
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
